lines: Commits: db1fe1c fix(android): publish the safe-area insets from MainActivity's listener; 0ad08cc fix(android): keep the safe-area bottom under a zero-inset keyboard (review N1 + N2, new commit, no amend). One file: frontend_stack_ts/android/app/src/main/java/com/beonedge/app/MainActivity.java. Not pushed, not landed. Review: .temp/p-safe-area-native/review.md (LAND).

Cause confirmed (STATIC): Bridge constructor -> registerAllPlugins -> SystemBars.load() -> initWindowInsetsListener sets the decor-view listener during super.onCreate; MainActivity then sets its own on the same view and replaces it (one listener per view). So the plugin's padding and injectSafeAreaCSS never run in this app.

Change: the existing decor listener still strips the IME inset and publishes --be-keyboard-height / be:keyboard unchanged, and now also writes --safe-area-inset-top|right|bottom|left on document.documentElement on every dispatch.

Values as SystemBars.injectSafeAreaCSS (8.5.3, lines 242-281): insets.getInsets(systemBars()|displayCutout()) of the incoming insets, (int)(px / density) truncation. One deliberate difference since 0ad08cc (N1): the bottom drops to 0 only when ime() is visible AND its bottom inset > 0 (plugin: whenever visible), so a floating/undocked keyboard or hardware-keyboard toolbar that reports visible with no inset keeps the nav's bottom padding. imeBottom is read once in the lambda and reused for publishKeyboardHeight (still keyboardVisible ? imeBottom : 0). Shared evaluateOnPage helper replaces the duplicated bridge null check.
No decor padding is restored: the WebView stays edge-to-edge and CSS applies the insets, as in the plugin's own WebView>=140 passthrough branch.

Comments corrected (rule 9), no new blocks: the listener block says it replaces the plugin's listener, that the plugin injects nothing, why this listener publishes the variables and (0ad08cc) the one difference from injectSafeAreaCSS; the insetsHandling 'css' reason (only then is the plugin's onPageCommitVisible requestApplyInsets hook registered); publishKeyboardHeight's comment no longer says 'matching how Capacitor injects' and (N2) says the plugin re-requests insets once the page commits, not on DOM ready.

Decision: publish on every WebView version, no version check. (1) On >=140 the plugin itself would publish these variables (passthrough branch calls injectSafeAreaCSS), and tokens-core.css reads the variable before env(). (2) Our listener passes system-bar and cutout insets to the WebView unchanged, so on >=140 env() and the variable come from the same insets: they differ by truncation (under 1 CSS px per side) and by the bottom under an open keyboard with an inset (variable 0; env() keeps the nav-bar height because Chromium never sees the IME). The 0 is better there: AUTH_SHELL pads by --be-keyboard-height (the IME inset, which already spans the nav bar) and AUTH_FOOTNOTE adds --be-safe-bottom, so env() counts the nav bar twice. (3) One path means the WebView 133 emulator runs the code phones run; no WebView version parsing.

Measured basis for 'below 140 env() leaves out the system bars': emu-test-0182 U2 (bottom 0 in gesture nav) and U4 (landscape top in the status-bar band); the portrait top of 51 px matches the cutout.
Rule 11: native-only, ships only in new APKs; no API, contract, data or persisted state; released APKs keep their own MainActivity; browser builds never run this code.
Tests: none. There are no unit tests for this Java file and rule 10 does not justify one (layout). No red control. Runtime check is the coordinator's, on the WebView 133 emulator.

Evidence at db1fe1c (clean tree, green): contracts npm ci && npm run build 7e67a708; frontend npm ci && npm run check 11722a3d (58 files, 511 tests); build:client + build:admin + build:android + build:android:admin 15d81bc6 (client dist 72 assets 982296 bytes, 61 chunks boot; admin 104 assets 1350291 bytes, 92 chunks boot; phonepe check passed both); host npm ci + cap sync android (client) + compileDebugJavaWithJavac a371df84 (task UP-TO-DATE from an identical trial) and the same with --rerun d6a60d36 (executed).

Evidence at 0ad08cc (clean tree, green): host ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac --rerun --no-daemon a94b4415 (task executed, 1 executed 93 up-to-date, BUILD SUCCESSFUL); container frontend npm ci && npm run check 0671774a (58 test files, 511 tests passed; check-bundle-boots 61 chunks; check-phonepe-native-target passed). The four builds were not re-run: 0ad08cc changes only the Java file, which no web build reads.

Compile notes: cap sync needs BOE_CAPACITOR_VARIANT and an existing dist (it used the container build:android:admin dist; irrelevant to javac). ~/.gradle/gradle.properties pins org.gradle.java.home=/opt/android-studio/jbr, so JAVA_HOME does not choose the JVM. Recorded runs used --no-daemon; no Gradle daemon left running. Admin variant not compiled separately: same Java source, identical plugin list. No device install, no adb.
Worktree node_modules are now container builds (last npm ci in the container); a host Gradle run needs a host npm ci first, as a371df84 did.
EMULATOR STEPS (both dev APKs built from 0ad08cc, WebView 133, navigation_mode=2, portrait 412x915, DevTools on each WebView):

1. Client, signed in, Home /dashboard. Console: ['top','right','bottom','left'].map(s => document.documentElement.style.getPropertyValue('--safe-area-inset-' + s)). Expect four non-empty values, bottom non-zero, equal to the gesture band (24px expected; 0.18.2 gave ''). Top about 51px (truncated whole px).

2. Same screen: getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('nav[aria-label="Sections"]')).paddingBottom equals the bottom value (0.18.2: 0px); its getBoundingClientRect() height grows by that amount and its bottom stays 915. Screenshot: the gesture handle runs through the nav's empty bottom band, below the labels; 'Portfolio' is not crossed (compare emu-run/contact_client1.png). getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--be-safe-bottom') resolves to the same value.

3. Admin, signed in, any tab root: the same three checks on nav[aria-label="Sections"]. 0.18.2: 56 px tall at 859-915; expect 56 + bottom inset (about 80 px, 835-915), labels clear of the handle (compare emu-run/admin_payout_form.png).

4. Client landscape: rotate, open the SIP detail used for emu-run/client_landscape_sip.png. Expect --safe-area-inset-top > 0 (status-bar height), the header's computed paddingTop = 8px + that inset, back chevron and bell drawn below the status bar; left or right inset non-zero on the cutout side. Rotate the other way and back to portrait: values update on each rotation and portrait returns to the step-1 values.

5. Keyboard: on the client sign-in screen, first run window.addEventListener('be:keyboard', e => console.log(e.detail)), then tap the email field. With a full on-screen keyboard: innerHeight unchanged, --be-keyboard-height and the logged height equal to the keyboard, --safe-area-inset-bottom 0px while it is open and back to the step-1 value after closing. On this AVD (hw.keyboard=yes, Gboard floating toolbar): --safe-area-inset-bottom must stay at the step-1 value while the toolbar shows (the N1 case), and the nav keeps its bottom padding; record --be-keyboard-height too.

DOUBTS: (1) Before the first publish lands (page commit), CSS falls back to env(): below 140 the bottom is 0 for the first frames, so a one-time shift at start is possible; on 140+ a sub-pixel shift. (2) On 140+ phones, under an open keyboard with an inset, the nav's bottom padding drops to 0 (hidden by the keyboard), and the sign-in footnote sits one nav-bar height lower above the keyboard than in 0.18.2: worth one look on the maintainer's phone.

(3) @capacitor/android is pinned at 8.5.3. An upgrade that sets SystemBars' listener after onCreate (for example in handleOnStart) would replace this one and silently lose both the IME strip and these variables; re-read SystemBars.java on any Capacitor upgrade. (4) Review N3 (one evaluateJavascript per dispatch instead of two) left as is, as the review suggested.

FINDING, outside this lane (UI recipes): CLIENT_HEADER (ui/recipes/shellClient.ts:11), the admin header (shellAdmin.ts:13), layout.ts:5-7, auth.ts and overlay.ts use px-[max(space,var(--be-safe-left))], which sets padding-right from the LEFT inset. In landscape with the cutout or 3-button nav on the right, the right inset is ignored, so the bell can sit under it. BOTTOM_NAV uses pl-safe-left pr-safe-right correctly. Check step 4 in both rotations; the owner is a UI lane (p-shell-polish or later).
